'''Thibault Damour''' ({{IPA|fr|tibo damuʁ|lang}}; born 7 February 1951) is a French physicist.

He was a permanent professor in theoretical physics at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] (IHÉS) from 1989 to 2022. Since then, he is professor emeritus.

An expert in general relativity, he has long taught this theory at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] (Ulm). He contributed greatly to the modelling of [[gravitational waves]] from compact [[Binary star|binary systems]], and with [[Alessandra Buonanno]], he invented the [[Effective one-body formalism|"effective one-body"]] approach to representing the orbital trajectories of [[binary black holes]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Buonanno |first1=A. |last2=Damour |first2=T. |date=1999-03-08 |title=Effective one-body approach to general relativistic two-body dynamics |journal=Physical Review D |volume=59 |issue=8 |article-number=084006 |arxiv=gr-qc/9811091 |bibcode=1999PhRvD..59h4006B |doi=10.1103/physrevd.59.084006 |issn=0556-2821 |s2cid=14951569}}</ref>

In 2021 he was awarded, with [[Alessandra Buonanno]], the [[List of Balzan Prize recipients|Balzan Prize]] for Gravitation: physical and astrophysical aspects<ref>[https://www.balzan.org/en/prizewinners/alessandra-buonanno-and-thibault-damour Balzan Prize 2021]</ref> as well as the Galileo Galilei Medal and the Dirac Medal of the ICTP, both also shared with [[Frans Pretorius]].
